newsitem.title: UK: OFT backs BSkyB rate card for cable firms.
newsitem.headline: OFT backs BSkyB rate card for cable firms.

text.p: Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) said on Monday it had approved a revised rate card for the supply of BSkyB channels to broadband cable operators.

BSkyB shares, firmer before the announcement, extended their gains to stand 22 1/2p higher at 499p at 1138 GMT. The satellite broadcaster gave informal undertakings to the Director General of Fair Trading, John Bridgeman, in July which included a requirement that it would revise the discount structure in its wholesale price list.
The Director General has approved the card following consultation with cable operators and further amendments agreed by BSkyB.
"The changes increase the flexibility of cable operators in marketing their services," Bridgeman said in a statement.
"The new rate card provides an element of choice on discounts and a new option to carry a basic Sky channel to less than 100 percent of subscribers," he added.

"The consultation produced few suggestions as to amendment of the detail of the card but some criticism that prices charged to cable are linked to the DTH (direct-to--home) price. The matter was considered during our review of BSkyB and pay television and since no evidence of adverse effects arising from the linkage was produced we concluded that no action was necessary," he added.
The rate card will be effective 60 days from today.

It gives cable operators the option to choose discount structures based either on the ratio of the number of premium channels taken to the number of premises which can be connected to cable or the ratio of the number of premium channels to basic channels taken.
Within each of these options, cable operators also have the alternative to choose either a grauduated discount structure or a flat rate charge for Sky Sports 3.
